Where to start

pdmS7 documentation

Source: vignettes/reading-paths.Rmd
reading-paths.Rmd

pdmS7 is a probability-distributed rainfall-runoff model (Moore, 2007) built for one purpose: to calibrate conceptual models fairly, record that calibration so it can be defended, and compare the result with machine-learning models on equal terms. Different readers need different parts. Pick the role closest to yours and read the articles in order. The Glossary explains any term along the way.

I calibrate models (Custodian)

  1. How the PDM works: what the model does, in plain English.
  2. Preparing your data: from EA sources to model files, with a checklist.
  3. Your first model run: data to a calibrated, saved model. Or, with no data to hand, Synthetic rivers.
  4. Starting a run and Choosing model components.
  5. Scoring a simulation: what each score shows.
  6. How automatic calibration works, including staged calibration.
  7. Calibration records: the record a Steward will review.
  8. How the model structure is chosen, when the standard PDM may not suit.
  9. Larger floods: extrapolation and the rating: what the held-back wettest years and the rating flag show.

For many catchments at once, add Calibrating many catchments. Troubleshooting covers the common errors.

I review and sign off calibrations (Steward)

  1. Reviewing a calibration: a Steward’s guide: what to look at and what should make you stop.
  2. Scoring a simulation: enough to read the report’s scores.
  3. Calibration records: how the record is built.
  4. Inside the logs: what the checksums prove.
  5. Larger floods: extrapolation and the rating: how to read the held-back years in the test.

I am accountable for a model’s use (Owner)

  1. This page and the Steward’s guide, for what sign-off means.
  2. The benchmark protocol, if the model is part of the comparison with machine learning.
  3. Calibration log design, for the governance decisions behind the log.

I forecast

  1. How the PDM works.
  2. Forecast updating: state correction and error prediction.
  3. AR and ARMA error correction, explained: what the IMFS coefficients mean.
  4. Testing forecasts with hindcasts: skill by lead time against persistence.
  5. Scoring a simulation, for the threshold scores POD, FAR and CSI.

I build the LSTM side of the comparison

  1. The benchmark protocol: data, periods, effort and scoring, fixed in advance.
  2. Scoring a simulation: the scoring function both models are judged by.
  3. Testing forecasts with hindcasts: how forecasts from any model are scored.
  4. How the PDM works, to know what the LSTM is up against.

I develop or maintain the package

  1. Model equations: every equation, with Moore’s numbering.
  2. The C core: speed, equivalence tests and use from other languages.
  3. The Guides menu: validation, source notes, benchmark timing and the roadmap.
  4. Further reading.
